items.item_text: Bachelors Degree and/or equivalent work experience.
Experience in financial analysis, forecasting and strategic planning to analyze and compile financial data and reports.

Experience with moderately complex budgets, accounting and personnel functions including detailed budget preparation, contract and grant budget proposals, purchasing, payroll, ledger reconciliation, and fiscal close.
Experience with federal and private compliance regulations governing grant budgeting, financial reporting, cost-sharing standards, cost allocation, and policies regarding use of grant funds.

Experience providing administrative support, such as, making travel arrangements; processing travel and entertainment reimbursements; making meeting arrangements; preparing agendas and minutes; scheduling rooms; preparing meeting materials; etc.
Experience writing and proofreading clear, grammatically accurate documents and email.

Under general supervision, provide extramural and general-fund account management, planning, and budgetary analysis; serve as the compliance officer for assigned contract and grant activity; and act as a resource to Principal Investigators, Program Coordinators, and Center managers. Independently gather and apply financial data and University financial management mechanisms to ensure comprehensive and accurate budget construction. Work with Academic Department Research Administrators to understand new proposals, analyze programmatic needs, and make recommendations. Assist COE Senior Research Administrator in financial analyses and commitment tracking. Assist with the development and implementation of financial analyst tools to support compliance and accuracy for all extramural account activity for the College of Engineering. Assist with graduate students, post-docs and visiting scholars, appointments, travel, and research needs. travel and group and program review meetings, PI and Program Coordinator travel, and research support for research centers within the College of Engineering Deans Office.
35% - Post-Award Extramural Services, Financial Management & Compliance
Computer skills to utilize various programs and software for word processing, spreadsheets, and website applications including the Microsoft Office Suite and Oracle products.
Knowledge and understanding of UC-wide and UC Davis policies and procedures surrounding purchasing, payroll, graduate student hiring and salaries/steps, and accounting.
Organizational and time management skills to establish goals, set priorities and manage deadlines; flexibility to change direction and adjust priorities as the executives' needs dictate.
